findings.description: Private org-linked idps are cached by getForLogin but skipped by login-cache invalidation, leaking hideOnLogin/linkOnly idps onto the login page. — WHAT: getLoginPredicate() defines an org-linked identity provider as a 'login idp' only when BROKER_PUBLIC=true, but getForLogin(ALL, organizationId) (and ORG_ONLY with an org id) includes org-linked idps based solely on ORGANIZATION_ID=organizationId, so private org idps are cached yet never invalidated when they change. WHY: a private org idp updated to hideOnLogin=true or linkOnly=true stays in the login cache (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early because the predicate is false for both original and updated), and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), so the hidden/link-only idp is still returned and rendered on the login page. HOW: make invalidation cover any idp that can appear in a getForLogin result (e.g. also invalidate for org-linked idps regardless of BROKER_PUBLIC, or simply always invalidate the login caches on update/remove), and/or defensively re-check hideOnLogin/linkOnly in the bean filter.

Login list cache accumulates one entry per organizationId inside a single cache object, growing memory with org count. — WHAT: the getForLogin cache key is (realm, FetchMode) only, and each distinct organizationId queried adds a new entry to IdentityProviderListQuery.searchKeys (via the else branch that copies the previous query and appends the new searchKey), with each ALL-mode entry duplicating the full realm-level idp set. WHY: in a realm with many organizations, a single cached IdentityProviderListQuery object grows to O(orgs x idps) and the per-org entries are recomputed/copied on every miss, unlike getByOrganization which uses a separate cache key per org id. HOW: consider keying the login cache by organizationId as well, or accept the bounded-but-growing map and document the memory bound.

Removing a client/role/group throws UnsupportedOperationException when V1 and V2 fine-grained-authz flags are both enabled. — WHAT: The removal-event listener is gated on the V1 feature flag (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) but the management() factory it calls returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 flag (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) is enabled, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled/roles().setPermissionsEnabled throw UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: When both flags are enabled (they are independent — MgmtPermissions constructor ORs them), removing any client, role, or group fires the event, dispatches to V2, and throws UnsupportedOperationException mid-transaction, aborting the removal. HOW: Skip the legacy cleanup when V2 is active, e.g. gate on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ && !ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` (or otherwise ensure the listener dispatches to the same V1/V2 path it is gated on).

Owner-filtered resource lookups use server.getId() while resources are created/retrieved with getClientId()/no owner, so permission evaluation can silently fail. — WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) looks up the per-client resource with findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) and hasPermission(String scope) looks up the 'Clients' resource-type resource with findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()), but resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with owner = resourceServer.getClientId() and the resource-type resource is located by getResourceTypeResource via the owner-less findByName(resourceServer, type.getType()). WHY: If the ResourceServer id differs from the owning client id, these owner-filtered lookups return null and every per-client / all-clients permission check silently evaluates as false (denial of legitimate access), even though the equivalent Users code path uses the owner-less overload. HOW: Use the owner-less findByName(server, name) overload (matching UserPermissionsV2 and getResourceTypeResource), or pass server.getClientId() as the owner to match the create() call.

findByType('Clients') may match no resources because client resources are created without a type attribute. — WHAT: getClientsWithPermission enumerates per-client resources via resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), which matches on the resource's `type` attribute, but per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) without setting a type. WHY: If client resources carry no type='Clients' attribute, findByType returns nothing and getClientsWithPermission returns an empty set, breaking the 'list clients the user can map roles to' flow. HOW: Set the resource type to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE when creating the resource in getOrCreateResource (or enumerate resources by another attribute that is actually populated).

findByName uses server.getId() as ownerId but V2 client resources are owned by server.getClientId(), so per-client permission lookups always miss. — WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) looks up the per-client resource with `findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, using the resource server's internal id as the ownerId, but V2 client resources are created with owner = `resourceServer.getClientId()` (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource line 342). WHY: the owner filter never matches, so the lookup always returns null and per-client permissions are never evaluated — hasPermission(client, …) silently falls through to the all-clients type resource, breaking every V2 per-client permission check (the same ownerId mismatch on line 244 breaks hasPermission(String) for the "Clients" type resource). HOW: match the 2-arg lookup used elsewhere for V2 (e.g. `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId())`, as UserPermissionsV2 does), or pass the stored owner `server.getClientId()`.

V2 client resources are created without a resource type, so findByType("Clients") in getClientsWithPermission never returns them. — WHAT: getClientsWithPermission enumerates client resources with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, …)`, but per-client resources created for the new CLIENTS type via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are never assigned a resource type (no `resource.setType(...)`; V1's ClientPermissions.initialize sets `resource.setType("Client")` explicitly). WHY: findByType on "Clients" returns no per-client resources, so getClientsWithPermission always yields an empty/incorrect set and any client-list filtering by granted scope silently shows nothing. HOW: set the resource type when creating V2 client resources (e.g. `resource.setType(resourceType)` in getOrCreateResource) so findByType can enumerate them.

Removal cleanup listener is gated on the V1 feature flag, so V2 mode never cleans up authorization resources for removed roles/clients/groups. — WHAT: the RoleRemoved/ClientRemoved/GroupRemoved cleanup listener is gated on `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (the V1 flag), while this PR adds the Client resource type to the V2 authorization schema. WHY: when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled (V1 flag disabled), the listener never fires, so `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` cleanup is skipped and authorization resources/policies for removed roles, clients, and groups are orphaned in V2 mode. HOW: also run the cleanup when the V2 feature flag is enabled and use a V2-compatible cleanup (ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the cleanup must delete the resource rather than call that method).

Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||, denying legitimate admins/owners. — WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` instead of `||`, so a user must be both a team admin AND a team owner to pass. WHY: `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` check distinct membership roles, so team admins (or owners) who hold only one role are rejected with FORBIDDEN, breaking the intended authorization gate. HOW: use `||`.

Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's. — WHAT: EventManager is constructed from the acting user (`...user`) and their credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`) even though `evt.destinationCalendar` points at the organizer's calendar and `booking.user.credentials` were fetched but never used. WHY: when an attendee or team admin (not the organizer) adds guests, `updateCalendarAttendees` runs against the organizer's destination calendar using the actor's credentials, so the calendar update fails or targets the wrong calendar. HOW: build EventManager with the organizer (or `booking.user`) and the organizer's credentials, not `ctx.user`.

Null booking.userId becomes id:0 and crashes findFirstOrThrow. — WHAT: `findFirstOrThrow` is called with `id: booking.userId || 0`, so a booking with a null `userId` (collective/team bookings without an assigned host) resolves to `id: 0`. WHY: `findFirstOrThrow` throws when no user has id 0, crashing the mutation for valid team bookings. HOW: guard against a null `booking.userId` (e.g., derive organizer from `booking.user` or throw a clear error) before the lookup.

Duplicate guest emails in input create duplicate attendee records. — WHAT: The `guests` input is filtered against existing attendees and the blacklist but not deduplicated against itself, and the schema (`z.array(z.string().email())`) permits duplicate emails. WHY: passing the same email twice inserts duplicate Attendee rows via `createMany`, contradicting the `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error intent. HOW: deduplicate and lowercase the input before filtering (e.g., `Array.from(new Set(guests.map((g) => g.toLowerCase())))`).

Case-sensitive blacklist/attendee comparison lets mixed-case emails bypass the filter. — WHAT: The blacklist is lowercased (line 71) but `guest` is compared without lowercasing (line 77), and the existing-attendee check (line 76) also compares case-sensitively. WHY: a blacklisted email with mixed casing bypasses the blacklist and is added as a guest, and an existing attendee with different casing is added as a duplicate. HOW: lowercase `guest` (and the attendee email) before comparison.

Add-guest emails are sent using the unfiltered guests list. — WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. WHY: `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts:541) emails every attendee whose email is in `newGuests`, so guests filtered out as already-existing attendees still receive a 'you were added as a guest' email even though they were not added. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests` instead.
